mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary conditions, which can lead to decreased corporate investments and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, indicating no negative impact.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in >60% of cases when UNRATE exceeds 5%, refuting the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with low unemployment indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, as tested by t-test p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >40% of cases during tightening, indicating no negative impact.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive in >50% of periods following increased housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production suggests strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days, but if INDPRO exceeds a certain threshold, it may indicate overheating and inflation, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >50% of cases when INDPRO exceeds 115, refuting the overheating signal.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment alongside low federal funds rates indicates a strong labor market and cheap capital, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not significantly positive when both conditions are met, as indicated by a t-test p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, increasing retail sales signal strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive in >50% of cases during late-cycle with high RSAFS growth.
